judges.1.p1.b2.text: Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?

judges.1.p1.b3.text: Judah shall go up, … Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.

judges.1.p1.b4.text: Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.

judges.1.p2.b5.text: When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands …

judges.1.p2.b6.text: As Adoni-bezek fled, they pursued him, seized him …

judges.1.p2.b7.text: Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.

judges.1.p3.b8.text: Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. … set it on fire.

judges.1.p3.b9.text: Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.

judges.1.p3.b10.text: Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron … and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

judges.1.p4.b11.text: To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.

judges.1.p4.b12.text: So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city …

judges.1.p4.b14.text: Give me a blessing, … Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.

judges.1.p5.b15.text: Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms … They went to live among the people.

judges.1.p5.b16.text: … and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.

judges.1.p5.b17.text: The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.

judges.1.p6.b18.text: The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.

judges.1.p6.b19.text: Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.

judges.1.p6.b20.text: … but released that man and all his family.

judges.1.p6.b21.text: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day.

judges.1.p7.b22.text: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, … for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.

judges.1.p7.b23.text: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.

judges.1.p7.b24.text: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.

judges.1.p8.b25.text: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

judges.1.p8.b26.text: … So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land …

judges.1.p8.b27.text: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.
